channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Turkmenistan for Meetings
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will travel to Turkmenistan for an official visit. He is scheduled to participate in the eighth Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan, as well as the upcoming CIS summit.

item.title: XX Youth Delphic Games of CIS Countries Open in Dushanbe
item.description: The XX Youth Delphic Games of the Commonwealth of Independent States have opened in Dushanbe. The opening ceremony took place at the Tajik State Academic Opera and Ballet Theater. The event aims to support young talents and preserve cultural heritage.

item.title: New Official to Oversee Economic Affairs in the Army
item.description: Tatiana Savelyeva is expected to manage the economic aspects of the army. Previously, she served as Vice Minister of Finance. Her predecessor, Asker Beisenov, also held a position in the Ministry of Defense's economics and finance department.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Serbia Agree on Mutual Military Product Supplies
item.description: Kazakhstan and Serbia have ratified an intergovernmental agreement on military-technical cooperation. The agreement, signed in November 2023, facilitates mutual supplies of military products, including armaments and equipment. This is expected to boost Kazakhstan's defense industry.

item.title: Regional Assemblies to Have Direct Link to Astana, Says Lawmaker
item.description: A new Council for Interaction with Regional Assemblies will establish direct communication with Astana, according to lawmaker Oleg Terenchenko. This structure aims to improve feedback on law development and monitoring, considering regional specifics. Participation will be voluntary and without state funding.

item.title: New Deputy Defense Minister Appointed in Kazakhstan
item.description: Tatiana Savelyeva has been appointed as the Deputy Minister of Defense of Kazakhstan. She previously resigned from her position as a member of the Kurultai. The appointment was made by the Head of State, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, according to the press service of Akorda.

item.title: Tatiana Savelyeva Becomes Deputy Defense Minister of Kazakhstan
item.description: Tatiana Savelyeva has been appointed as the Deputy Minister of Defense of Kazakhstan. She previously resigned from her position as a member of the Kurultai. The appointment was made by Head of State Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, according to the press service of Akorda.

item.title: Asker Beisenov Dismissed as Deputy Defense Minister of Kazakhstan
item.description: Asker Beisenov has been dismissed from his post as Deputy Minister of Defense of Kazakhstan, according to Akorda. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev signed the order. The reasons for the personnel decision were not disclosed. Beisenov held the position since April 2023.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Introduce New State Awards: Shamshi Kaldyabayev Medal and Honored Artist Title
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to introduce two new state awards: the "Shamshi Kaldyabayev" medal and the honorary title "Honored Artist of Kazakhstan." The proposed legislation, supported in its first reading, aims to recognize citizens who have significantly contributed to the development of national music and visual arts.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Supply Fuel to Central Asian Nations by 2030
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to meet its domestic fuel needs and begin exporting refined petroleum products to Central Asian countries by 2030. The nation is expanding existing refinery capacities and preparing to build a fourth refinery. The Energy Ministry stated that current refineries cover over 90% of domestic demand, with efforts underway to address aviation fuel shortages.

item.title: Almaty Mountain Cluster Development Enters New Phase for Mountain Tourism
item.description: The comprehensive plan for developing the Almaty mountain cluster includes 73 measures, with 49 to be implemented this year. The first phase focuses on modernizing the Shymbulak mountain resort and developing the Butakht and Kimasar gorges. Future plans include connecting the Oi-Qaragai and Pioneer resorts via cable cars by 2027.

item.title: Barqi Tojik Discusses Continued Electricity Exports to Afghanistan with Brezno Company
item.description: Barqi Tojik confirmed discussions with the Brezno company regarding the continuation of electricity exports to Afghanistan. However, the company stated that an increase in electricity exports was not discussed during the meeting. Further details were not provided.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev to Visit Turkmenistan October 7-9
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will pay a working visit to Turkmenistan from October 7-9 at the invitation of President Serdar Berdimuhamedov. He will attend the 8th consultative meeting of Central Asian and Azerbaijani leaders in the Avaza tourist zone and the CIS summit. Discussions will cover regional cooperation, economy, energy, and security.

item.title: Kazakhstan Renews Oil Supply Agreement with Russia Until 2028
item.description: Kazakhstan has ratified a protocol to renew its oil and petroleum product supply agreement with Russia. The agreement, which expired on January 1, 2024, is extended until January 1, 2028, with automatic five-year renewals thereafter unless terminated by either party. This renewal aims to foster further trade and economic cooperation in the energy sector between the two nations.

item.title: Atyrau Refinery Denies Lack of Emission Calculations for Certain Units
item.description: The Atyrau Oil Refinery (AOR) disputes the Ministry of Ecology's claim of missing emission calculations for specific technological furnaces. AOR states it possesses valid calculations within its environmental permit, covering fuel and natural gas combustion. The refinery asserts that emission standards for these sources are established according to approved methodologies and is prepared to provide supporting documentation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Biometric Verification for Youth Money Transfers
item.description: A proposal has been made in Kazakhstan to introduce additional biometric identification for money transfers made by individuals aged 14 to 22. The suggestion aims to combat the issue of young people renting out their bank accounts for illicit financial operations. The proposal also calls for improved preventative education in educational institutions and better information exchange between banks and law enforcement.

item.title: Council for Interaction with Maslikhats to be established under Kurultai
item.description: A Council for Interaction with Maslikhats (local representative bodies) will be established under the Kurultai (national assembly). This initiative aims to improve cooperation between the legislative body and regional administrations.

item.title: Uzbekistan's September inflation rate reaches 0.7%, year-to-date at 4.2%
item.description: Inflation in Uzbekistan reached 0.7% in September, the highest monthly rate since January, according to the National Statistics Committee. Year-to-date inflation stands at 4.2%, with annual inflation slowing to 6.4%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Building Fourth Oil Refinery in Three Regions
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering several sites in the Atyrau, Ulytau, and Mangystau regions for a potential fourth oil refinery. A feasibility study is planned by the end of the year. The country currently has three major refineries and 25 mini-refineries, but faces challenges with aviation fuel supply and the quality of products from smaller facilities.

item.title: Shymkent Murder Trial: Prosecutor Seeks Severe Sentences for Six Defendants
item.description: In the Shymkent murder case of Vasily Kolesnikov, the prosecutor requested severe sentences for six defendants. The prosecution seeks 22 to 24 years imprisonment for each, and 10 million tenge in moral damages for the victim, Koshkinbayev. Defendants and their lawyers deny murder and attempted murder charges, arguing insufficient evidence.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Extend Agreement on Oil Product Supplies
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia are extending their agreement on oil and petroleum product supplies until January 1, 2028, with automatic five-year renewals. The protocol ensures continued coordination between competent authorities, information exchange, and monitoring of oil product usage, preventing potential deficits and maintaining a duty-free regime.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy: Counterterrorism Cannot Justify Civilian Attacks or Territorial Violations
item.description: Afghanistan's acting UN envoy, Nasir Ahmad Faiq, stated that counterterrorism efforts cannot justify attacks on civilians or violations of territorial integrity. He condemned terrorism in all forms and called for accountability for groups providing support to terrorists. Faiq also condemned Pakistani airstrikes, citing civilian casualties.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Healthcare Ministry Spends Trillions on Free Medications
item.description: Over three million Kazakhstanis annually receive free medications funded by the state. Over seven years, the budget for this purpose has tripled, reaching 272.9 billion tenge by 2025, with total spending hitting 1.3 trillion tenge. The Ministry of Health has increased direct purchases from manufacturers and through international organizations to save costs and prevent shortages.

item.title: Astana parking fire victim in intensive care
item.description: A victim of a parking lot fire near a residential complex in Astana is in intensive care. The fire, which occurred on October 6, involved five cars burning with open flames. Strong winds reportedly spread the fire to adjacent vehicles. The patient's condition is described as serious but stable.

item.title: Fire safety rules to follow when heating homes
item.description: With colder weather approaching, the Ministry of Emergency Situations reminds citizens to follow fire safety rules. These include checking heating devices and electrical networks for proper functioning, not leaving lit stoves or heaters unattended, avoiding overloading electrical systems, and not using homemade heaters. Regular chimney cleaning is also advised.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai Establishes New Council to Involve Local Assemblies in Lawmaking
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai has established a new council to enhance interaction with local assemblies (maslikhats). This council aims to strengthen ties between regions and central government bodies, allowing maslikhats to participate in drafting legislation and provide feedback on its implementation. The council will meet biannually and include representatives from various government levels and political parties.

item.title: Oil Tanker Attacked in Strait of Hormuz; Oman Evacuates 10 Injured Crew Members
item.description: An oil tanker passing through the Strait of Hormuz was attacked, injuring 12 crew members. Oman's air force evacuated 10 of the injured to a hospital. The Panamanian-flagged vessel, 'Ann Peace,' was carrying 19 crew members when an unknown projectile hit it, causing a fire.

item.title: Kazakhstan Orders Deportation of Russian Soldier Who Fled Military Service
item.description: A court in Kazakhstan's West Kazakhstan region has ordered the deportation of a Russian soldier who illegally crossed the border after deserting the Russian army. He was apprehended attempting to reach a third country. The court fined him but waived the penalty due to amnesty.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to 4.5 Years for Fighting in Russia-Ukraine War
item.description: A 38-year-old Uzbek citizen, identified as A.N., has been sentenced to 4.5 years in prison for participating in the Russia-Ukraine war on the Russian side. He fought in Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kherson regions. A.N. deserted and returned to Uzbekistan after falsifying travel documents, facing administrative charges before his sentencing.

item.title: Man Arrested for Marrying and Abusing a Minor in Tashkent
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent's Olmazor district have identified a man who married a minor and subjected her to sexual violence. The National Social Protection Agency reported that the man entered into a religious marriage with the underage girl and lived with her, causing her physical harm. An investigation is underway.

item.title: British Special Forces May Face Prosecution for Alleged Afghanistan Crimes
item.description: The UK Ministry of Defence has identified material suggesting British service personnel may have committed serious offenses in Afghanistan, including murder and manslaughter. UK Special Forces referred this information to the Defence Serious Crime Command earlier this year. A High Court hearing in London was informed of these developments.

item.title: Pakistan Spokesperson: Taliban Have No Right to Lecture on Democracy
item.description: Pakistan's presidential spokesperson stated that the Taliban, who seized power through violence, have no authority to lecture Pakistan on democracy. He accused the Taliban of violating the Doha Agreement and stripping Afghan women of their rights. The spokesperson highlighted the contradiction of a regime legitimized by force questioning a democratic country.

item.title: Afghan Agriculture Minister Attends Food Security Forum in Tashkent
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Agriculture, Irrigation, and Livestock, Attaullah Omari, is in Tashkent to attend an international forum on food security and sustainable development. The visit, at Uzbekistan's invitation, aims to discuss expanding bilateral and regional cooperation in agriculture and related sectors.

item.title: Kazakh Citizens Recruited for War in Russia Seek Help Returning Home
item.description: Kazakh citizens recruited for the war in Russia claim they were threatened with imprisonment and forced to sign contracts after going to Russia for work. They are now seeking assistance to return to their homeland. Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has responded to the situation.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy: No Distinction Between 'Good' and 'Bad' Terrorists
item.description: Afghanistan's UN envoy, Naseer Ahmad Faiq, stated that terrorism in all its forms is condemned and no distinction should be made between 'good' and 'bad' terrorists. He emphasized that Afghanistan has suffered greatly from terrorism and the use of extremist groups as proxies. Faiq also criticized Pakistan's attacks on Afghan soil as illegal, regardless of counter-terrorism claims.

item.title: ICC Prosecutor: Arrest Warrants for Taliban Officials Vindicate Afghan Women's Rights
item.description: The International Criminal Court prosecutor's office stated that arrest warrants for Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada and three other officials vindicate the rights of Afghan women and girls, particularly their right to education. The warrants are for alleged persecution on gender and political grounds, a crime against humanity. The court issued warrants in 2025.

item.title: Tajikistan: Man Arrested for Fraud Involving Job Offers and Agricultural Equipment
item.description: In the Lakhsh district, police arrested a local man suspected of fraud. He allegedly took 50,000 somoni promising employment and later another 305,000 somoni for agricultural equipment, failing to fulfill either promise. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported the suspect returned part of the money.

item.title: New 110 kV Substation Inaugurated in Hamadoni District, Tajikistan
item.description: A new 110 kV "Chubek" substation has been commissioned in the Mir Sayid Alii Hamadoni district of Tajikistan. Built by "Electric Networks Distribution", it aims to strengthen the district's energy infrastructure and improve power supply reliability for residents and facilities. A new 14.5 km, 110 kV power line connects it to the national grid.

item.title: UN Chief: Afghan returns from Pakistan must be voluntary and safe
item.description: UN Secretary-General Guterres stated that Afghan returns from Pakistan must be voluntary, safe, and dignified. The UN remains committed to working with Pakistan to uphold protection principles for returning Afghans.

item.title: Man arrested in Andijan for counterfeiting 297 million Uzbek soums
item.description: A person was apprehended in Andijan while attempting to sell counterfeit banknotes totaling 297 million Uzbek soums for 148 million soums. The fake currency consisted of 100,000 and 200,000 soum denominations.
